title: Printable learner fieldbook
lead: Paper sheets for observation, physical progression, arguments, experiments, useful work and reflection.
note: HTML reading edition from the same source as the PDF. Printed pages and screen sections can differ in pagination.

sections.title: A question. A notebook. A beginning.

blocks.html: Use this paper fieldbook during the offline Jasper Field Semester. Print additional copies of the route, laboratory and reading sheets as needed. Keep private reflection separate from assessed evidence.

blocks.text: Name / chosen identifier
My question for this semester
A strength I bring; someone my learning could help

blocks.html: Proposed program: 6 weeks in Jasper; 144 facilitated + 24 independent-study hours. Adults aged 18+. Delivery remains unconfirmed. No degree or academic credit. English edition: 15 October 2026.

Personal phones, internet and live AI are off during teaching and camps, with agreed private medical, accessibility and essential-contact exceptions. Staff emergency communications remain active. Storage is voluntary and devices are returned on request. Agree the arrangement before formal registration opens.

blocks.text: My purpose and an observable sign of progress
A useful adaptation or alternative I choose to share
Weekly evidence tracker: 1 Attention / 2 Discipline / 3 Evidence / 4 Freedom / 5 Responsibility / 6 Contribution

blocks.html: Private health details belong in the agreed confidential process, never in this portfolio. Do not grade beliefs, physique or private experiences.

sections.title: Read the place. Plan the return.

blocks.html: Complete with the responsible guide before an authorized outing. This sheet does not approve a route. Make a fresh copy for each trip.

blocks.text: Date / staff / route / current information checked and time
Map scale / distance / elevation / time range / assumptions
Weather, access, kit and communications checked; turnaround and exit plan
A decision we changed, the evidence and the result

blocks.html: Any learner may ask for a stop. The guide controls route decisions. Use indoor equivalents when essential conditions are not met.

sections.title: Make a camp work for everyone.

blocks.html: Record the actual authorized site, planned night(s), staff coverage and access arrangements. Record a day-camp equivalent honestly if no overnight is completed.

blocks.text: Site / booking checked by staff / people / dates
Shelter, attractant storage, water, toilets, food and waste plan
Fair roles / quiet hours / help and exit arrangements
What worked; what I would change before the next camp

blocks.html: No activity depends on campfires, foraging or remote survival. Follow the actual site rules and responsible guide.

Complete with the qualified coach. Twelve 30-minute sessions sit within the 36-hour field course. Choose submaximal practice, record technique and recovery privately, and progress one suitable variable when appropriate.

blocks.text: Week 1 baseline: task, support, effort, technique and conditions
Session log: date / practice / feedback / next adjustment
Week 6 comparison: what changed; what could explain it?

blocks.html: No maximal test or public fitness ranking. Stop for pain, dizziness, distress or loss of control; follow the coach and agreed response plan. This sheet is not a prescription.

Practise only with the qualified coach. Agree touch, partner and intensity each time. Stop on request or discomfort; tell the coach about an injury. No head strikes, hard sparring, chokes, submissions or uncoached takedowns.

blocks.text: My chosen adaptation / stop signal / approved practice
Twelve-session record: date, skill, coach feedback, next adjustment
A decision to use restraint, and why it mattered

blocks.html: Completion means a coached introductory demonstration of control. It is not a belt, fighting licence or promise of self-defence capability.
Use short meditation, quiet drawing, reading or another agreed attention practice. Eyes can stay open. Stop or change an uncomfortable exercise. Share only what you choose.

blocks.text: Method A / setting / duration / observation
Method B / setting / duration / observation
What might explain the difference? What remains uncertain?
My preferred method, alternative and stop condition

blocks.html: One experience does not support a general health claim. Inner experiences, stillness and personal disclosures are not assessment scores.
Print one copy for each investigation. Distinguish real measurements from supplied illustrative data. Do not discard a result because it disagrees with the prediction.

blocks.text: Question / prediction / a result that would challenge it
Variables / controls / method / equipment / boundaries
Raw data with units, repeated trials and instrument resolution
Conclusion / uncertainty / alternative explanation

blocks.html: A peer should be able to follow the method. Keep original data and show later corrections without hiding the first entry.
Show assumptions, definitions, units and intermediate steps. Label axes and scale. A correct answer still needs a defensible method.

blocks.text: Model, calculation or geometric argument
Graph / labelled diagram

blocks.html: Identify which claims follow mathematically from assumptions and which depend on uncertain measurements.

sections.title: Meet the argument on its terms.

blocks.html: Print a copy for each text. Use the actual assigned edition. Distinguish the author’s claim from your interpretation; keep a precise passage reference.

blocks.text: Author / title / edition / passage / historical context
The central claim and the strongest supporting reason
An assumption, a key term and an interpretive uncertainty
My objection; a passage that could challenge my reading

blocks.html: Do not make different traditions agree by replacing their arguments with a common slogan.

Use this sheet for tutorial and essay revision. Preserve a precise passage, a serious objection and your answer. Two essays of 1,200–1,500 words each or agreed equivalents develop across the semester.

blocks.text: Motion / my initial claim / passage evidence
The strongest opposing argument and why it has force
What I changed after switching sides
A revised claim and an unresolved question

blocks.html: The aim is a clearer judgment, not a public winner. Record a fair contribution, not speaking volume or confidence.
Work in pairs; keep individual reasoning visible. Obtain consent for feedback. Label peer feedback as peer feedback when no local host participates.

blocks.text: User / question / artefact / evidence needed
Version 1 test: what worked, failed and needs revision
Version 2: feedback acted on; cost, access and trade-offs
My contribution; the evidence that someone can use it

blocks.html: A paper guide, model, route-decision worksheet or reader can be a substantial contribution when tested and explained well.

sections.title: What can I now explain, do and give?

blocks.html: Collect six weekly entries, two revised essays, an 800–1,200-word scientific dossier or equivalent, useful original work and reviewed physical, field and martial demonstrations. Use the five-dimension rubric and revise missing evidence.

blocks.text: Evidence: practice / reasoning / argument / original work / contribution
Oral defence: my claim, strongest objection and justified revision
A realistic 30-day commitment, resources and next review

blocks.html: English edition: 15 October 2026. Founding vision and original crest: Vincent Zhang. Keep private reflection separate. Completion is a descriptive non-credit record.
Use after the offline semester in a separately arranged three-hour lab. Choose non-sensitive preserved work. Record model, date, prompt, output and any tool access. Do not upload private information.

blocks.text: Original work and criteria set before viewing output
Model contribution and consequential claims to verify
Verification: sources, calculations, errors and uncertainties
My final judgment, revision and disclosure

blocks.html: Optional and outside the 168 academic hours. One classroom comparison cannot establish general model rankings.

Educator-created data, not field measurements. Room: 20°C. Minutes: 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. Cup A °C: 40, 36, 33, 30, 28. Cup B °C: 40, 38, 36.5, 35, 33.5. One demonstration per condition; A unwrapped, B candidate wrap.

blocks.text: Calculate 20-minute temperature drops and their difference; show units
Graph temperature above ambient or compare interval rates
Challenge this claim: the wrap keeps hikers safe
Revise the conclusion; design a repeatable next test

blocks.html: Worked check: drops 12°C and 6.5°C; final-temperature difference 5.5°C. These synthetic unreplicated values cannot establish a causal effect or outdoor performance.
